camps.name: Silver Lake camp
camps.why: Needs the water-taxi or Silver Creek approach, so far fewer parties use it. The glacier toe is closer, but most go via Depot Creek and sleep at Ouzel Lake instead.

camps.name: Ouzel Lake camp
camps.why: Where nearly everyone sleeps: the Depot Creek hike ends here, and the Silver Glacier is a day trip from the lake via the pass toward Silver Lake.

plan_conflict: Camp on file lists Silver Lake as the main camp, but climbers' reports camp at Ouzel Lake via Depot Creek; Ouzel Lake is made the main camp.

camps.name: Ouzel Lake
camps.why: The standard base: reached in six to seven hours via Depot Creek, with Spickard about three hours above camp, and it also serves Redoubt and the Moxes.

camps.name: Lower Depot Creek bench
camps.why: Not slept at on a normal trip. It is a fallback for a slow day on the falls headwall, or a short last stop on the way out.

camps.name: Ouzel Lake basin, head of Depot Creek
camps.why: Reached after a slow, brushy day up Depot Creek; the last flat sandy benches before the glacier, so parties sleep here before moving up to the saddle.

new_camps.name: Redoubt Glacier high camp
new_camps.why: Rocky knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier. It cuts the Mox summit day to a manageable length compared with climbing from Ouzel Lake.
new_camps.notes: A knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier near 7,200 ft with views south, used as the base for the Mox peaks. Some parties instead bivy at Redoubt Col nearby.

plan_conflict: Strong parties and some reports skip the second camp (Redoubt Col bivy or a same-day exit); the plan's night 2 and 3 high camp is not on file, so it is added.

new_camps.name: Ouzel Lake camp
new_camps.why: The usual first night: the Depot Creek hike ends at the lake and parties rest before hauling loads up to the Redoubt Glacier.
new_camps.notes: Sandy benches by the lake at about 5,700 ft, the standard camp for the Chilliwack peaks. Some parties camp here two nights.

new_camps.name: Redoubt Glacier high camp
new_camps.why: Rocky knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier. It cuts the Mox summit day to a manageable length compared with climbing from Ouzel Lake.
new_camps.notes: A knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier near 7,200 ft with views south, used as the base for the Mox peaks. Some parties instead bivy at Redoubt Col nearby.

camps.name: Ouzel Lake camp
camps.why: Where the Depot Creek hike ends; parties sleep here the first night and carry up to the glacier saddle next day, rather than doing everything in one push.

new_camps.why: Rocky knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier. It cuts the Mox summit day to a manageable length compared with climbing from Ouzel Lake.
new_camps.notes: A knoll at the head of the Redoubt Glacier near 7,200 ft with views south, used as the base for the Mox peaks. Some parties instead bivy at Redoubt Col nearby.

camps.name: Perry Creek basin
camps.why: The only camp area on file for the approach drainage; the wall bivy and the return are dispersed sites in the same basin, with no separately known camp for each night.

plan_conflict: Day 3 ends on a bivy ledge on the face, which is not a researched camp; night 3 is assigned to Perry Creek basin only so every night has a main, and no source confirms where nights 1 to 5 fall.

camps.name: Eldorado-Inspiration snow arm high camp
camps.why: The usual base for Austera: a short day from the trailhead, comfortable ground, and the Klawatti Glacier approach starts from here.

camps.name: Klawatti Col camp
camps.why: Trims the Austera day and suits parties adding Klawatti or Dorado Needle, but costs a long glacier carry and is rarely used on a simple trip.

camps.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps.why: Roadside campground for the night before; lets you start walking early without a long drive from Marblemount.

camps.name: Eldorado East Ridge rock bivies
camps.why: Bare rock where snow has retreated; used only when the snow arm is too soft or crevassed to pitch on.

camps.name: Eldorado Basin camp
camps.why: A bail-out camp for parties who start late or find the boulder field slow, leaving a longer day to the glacier camp.

camps.name: Roush Creek Basin camp
camps.why: An alternative low camp when Eldorado Basin is crowded; adds distance to the glacier but is quieter.

plan_conflict: Klawatti Col camp and Marble Creek Campground are filed as main, but only the Eldorado camp fits a 3-day plan's nights 1 and 2; both are changed to route.

camps.name: Thunder Basin Hiker Camp
camps.why: Meadow camp below Park Creek Pass, a base for the Booker-Buckner col; camping is banned at the pass itself, so this and nearby knolls are used.

camps.name: Neve Camp
camps.why: Under two miles in; only for a very late start, as it leaves a punishing second day to the pass area.

camps.name: Junction Camp
camps.why: About ten miles in; a way to split the long approach into two days for a four-day trip, with the Fisher Basin trail starting here.

camps.name: Skagit Queen Camp
camps.why: Last creekside camp before the climb toward the pass; splits the approach if the first day starts late.

camps.name: Five Mile Camp, Park Creek trail
camps.why: Camp on the east side of Park Creek Pass; used by parties who come in from the Stehekin side instead of Thunder Creek.

plan_conflict: The plan's day 1 puts a party near Park Creek Pass, which is a long day up Thunder Creek; many parties actually split the approach and camp on a knoll near 6,000 ft southwest of the pass.

camps.name: Boston Basin upper (high) camp
camps.why: The high camp near 6,400 ft; parties pitch here and the climb is a short half-day above camp, with a toilet and a higher start.

camps.name: Boston Basin lower camp
camps.why: Lower, more sheltered and melts out sooner, so it suits early season or slower arrivals, but adds a longer morning to the route.

plan_conflict: Both Boston Basin camps are filed as main; only the high camp fits the plan, so the lower camp is changed to route.

camps.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps.why: The practical base for Boston: the Quien Sabe Glacier starts right above, so the 10-12 hour summit day begins close to the snow.

camps.name: Boston Basin low camp
camps.why: Melts out sooner and is more sheltered, so slower parties and early-season trips use it, at the cost of a longer summit day.

camps.name: Boston Basin upper (high) camp
camps.why: Closest camp to Sharkfin Col and the start of the ridge, which matters on a roughly 13-hour day; has a toilet and snow-melt water.

camps.name: Boston Basin lower camp
camps.why: Sheltered and snow-free early, but adds a long hike to the ridge on an already very long day.

camps.name: Informal snow and rock bivouacs above the basins
camps.why: Not a planned camp. Parties who run out of daylight on the ridge or traverse end up here and sleep there.

plan_conflict: The route is usually climbed mid-traverse (Sharkfin Tower or Forbidden Peak toward Boston and Sahale), so nights may fall at bivouacs on the ridge or at Sahale instead.

camps.name: Boston Glacier bivy
camps.why: Exposed glacier camp that puts the face a short walk away, used by two-day parties; you sleep on a crevassed surface with no shelter.

camps.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps.why: More comfortable sandy flats below the snowfield but a long carry from the face; fine for a slow first day before moving up.

camps.name: Sahale–Boston col bivy
camps.why: A tiny perch on the col, used when linking the face with other climbs or when weather forces a stop.

new_camps.name: Sahale Glacier Camp
new_camps.why: Where the descent from the summit ends before the Cascade Pass exit; flat moraine ground shortens the last day.
new_camps.notes: At the end of the Sahale Arm trail near 7,600-7,700 ft; the standard camp for the southwest side of Buckner. Permits go fast on summer weekends.

plan_conflict: The camp on file lists Boston Basin high camp as main, but the plan's night 1 is a Boston Glacier camp and night 2 is at Sahale or Horseshoe Basin; Boston Basin high camp is changed to route.

camps.name: Sahale Glacier Camp
camps.why: The standard base for Buckner from the southwest: about six miles from Cascade Pass, with the summit slopes reached through Horseshoe Basin.

camps.name: Upper Horseshoe Basin bivy
camps.why: An alternative for parties who cannot get a Sahale Glacier Camp permit, sleeping on whatever flat ground the upper basin offers.
